reviews.title: It’s fun, but its not dialed in
reviews.text:
The point of this app is to keep you engaged in a reward system program. The days you schedule your workout, the app will give you a program to complete. If you don’t do it, you get penalized (in leveling points) the UI is nice, but it needs more user interaction functions. 

I bought the yearly plan to give this a fair review. Anything above E rank is not available, they have not released the programs as of the date of this review. S rank is available, but you have to be in great shape to attempt them.

Some improvement to suggest.

When asking users what their workout experience is like, keep the program according to their selection. 
A novice, or someone who is not active will usually be unable to doing clapping pushups, tri angle pushups, or even archer pushups. 

Asking users what equipment they have available, and not keeping the workouts consistent. 
If the user chooses no equipment, why put bench press, dumbbells, or even kettle bells in their quest? To be fair, You are able to swap out the workouts. But, they aren’t suggested workouts, you have to determine if the newly chosen workout (with limited selection) will be a good substitute.

Create a way to view your previous workouts and choose/save the ones you enjoy. 

Achievements, describe how we are able to complete them.

I believe they are still in BETA release. Hope they continue to succeed with newer updates

reviews.title: We need more
reviews.text:
Hey this app is awesome, and gamifies weight-lifting without making it corny.
There are two aspects that I feel this app is lacking in heavily.
1. This app *needs* an online ranking system. Without it, there is no real challenging yourself by getting more points/ levels than others.
2. Adding the ability to track if you have/ have not hit your macro goals in the app would add another large pull towards using the app. With that, the app would feel like an entire Bobdybuilding/ Health ecosystem, not just an app to track workouts

My BMI is 18.4 underweight in reality. 
On top of this it told me my goal of 125 would be a lower BMI than where I am at 100.
These extreme inaccuracies are unacceptable.

I was hoping this app would be of the same quality as other paid fitness apps with the added benefit of a very cool UI/UX but unfortunately they lean heavily on the solo leveling connection and less on being a robust fitness and lifestyle tool. I’ve been using the app for almost 7 weeks and have logged 28 workouts. Over the 7 weeks I have submitted a handful of feature requests and reached out regarding issues with my account login - I have received no response to any of my messages. I can only assume this app is a money grab banking on the relevance of Solo Leveling. It pains me to say it because I wanted so badly for this to be the one fitness app to rule them all. Unfortunately it is not. 2/5 stars because the UI/UX is well done.
